basics.title: Foundations before the journey
basics.description: Learn the obligation, the categories of Hajj, and the difference between foundational rulings and personal cases that still require a scholar.

umrah.title: Umrah step by step
umrah.description: The Umrah sequence is short, but mistakes usually happen through haste, crowd pressure, or uncertainty at the miqat and during tawaf.

conclusion.title: After Umrah
conclusion.text: When the hair is trimmed or shaved, Ihram ends. For Tamattu', the pilgrim remains out of Ihram until entering Ihram again for Hajj on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah.

hajj.title: The major days of Hajj
hajj.description: The order of the days matters, but the greatest misunderstanding is forgetting that Arafah is the center of the pilgrimage.

farewell.title: Farewell Tawaf
farewell.text: Before leaving Makkah, the pilgrim makes a final tawaf unless exempted by a recognized reason such as menstruation. Keep the ending dignified and avoid turning it into a rushed photo stop.

mistakes.title: Common mistakes to avoid
mistakes.description: These are recurring problems that do not come from lack of sincerity, but from poor preparation, pressure, and imitation without knowledge.

health.title: Health, safety, and readiness
health.description: Physical ability and official health requirements are part of real-world Hajj preparation, not an afterthought. Recheck them close to travel because they can change.
health.note: Official vaccination rules, seasonal public-health measures, and entry conditions must be checked against the Saudi Ministry of Health and Nusuk near departure.

rules.title: Ihram rules and etiquette
rules.description: Know the difference between what remains permitted, what is prohibited, and what should be taken to a scholar when an error happens.
rules.note: If an error happened because of illness, forgetfulness, or necessity, do not improvise the ruling. Ask a qualified scholar about validity, fidyah, and what must be repeated.

spiritual.title: Spiritual preparation
spiritual.description: The outward rites are stronger when repentance, humility, patience, and learning have already started before travel.

shorts.title: Short visual refreshers
shorts.description: These short videos are supplementary visual refreshers only. They are not the standard for legal rulings. Keep the Qur'an, hadith, and the PDF guides below above any short clip.

resources.title: Key references and official resources
resources.description: These are intentionally displayed as non-clickable reference blocks, with one reference per card, so the page behaves more like a study guide than a link directory. The PDF buttons above remain downloadable.

postHajj.title: Returning home with acceptance in mind
postHajj.description: The journey is not measured by photographs or stories, but by repentance, steadier prayer, better conduct, and a sincere hope that Allah accepted it.

summary.title: A concise end summary
summary.description: Use this as a fast recap after reading the full guide, not as a replacement for the primary texts, the PDF guides, or a scholar in personal cases.

basicsCards.title: Hajj is obligatory for the one who is able
basicsCards.desc: The obligation is tied to ability: physical capacity, financial capacity, and a workable route to the pilgrimage.

basicsCards.title: Umrah is not casual travel
basicsCards.desc: The Qur'an joins Hajj and Umrah in one verse, and the jurists discuss its exact legal weight. In any case, it is a legislated act of worship, not tourism.

basicsCards.title: Accepted Hajj brings immense reward
basicsCards.desc: The Prophet taught that an accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise, and one Umrah to the next expiates what came between them.

basicsCards.title: Learning the rites is part of the rite
basicsCards.desc: A pilgrim should not rely on crowd movement alone. Study before travel and ask when the issue affects validity or fidyah.

hajjTypes.title: Tamattu'
hajjTypes.desc: Perform Umrah in the months of Hajj, leave Ihram, then re-enter Ihram for Hajj on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah.
hajjTypes.note: Often the clearest path for many first-time pilgrims.

hajjTypes.title: Qiran
hajjTypes.desc: Enter Ihram for Umrah and Hajj together and remain in Ihram until the major rites are completed.
hajjTypes.note: Useful in some travel plans, but it keeps the pilgrim in Ihram longer.

hajjTypes.title: Ifrad
hajjTypes.desc: Enter Ihram for Hajj alone without combining Umrah into the same Ihram.
hajjTypes.note: The practical choice depends on circumstances, group planning, and fiqh guidance.

umrahSteps.title: Enter Ihram at the miqat
umrahSteps.desc: Make intention and begin Talbiyah at or before the appointed miqat. Do not cross the miqat casually and plan to fix it later.
umrahSteps.tip: Prepare clothing and intention before reaching the boundary if you are flying or moving with a group.

umrahSteps.title: Perform Tawaf with calmness
umrahSteps.desc: Circle the Kaaba seven times, beginning from the Black Stone area. The purpose is worship, not speed or crowd aggression.
umrahSteps.tip: If reaching the Black Stone is difficult, pointing from a distance is enough. Do not harm others.
umrahSteps.ref: Reference: General Prophetic rite sequence and the instruction to learn the rituals in Sunan an-Nasa'i 3062.

umrahSteps.title: Complete Sa'i between Safa and Marwah
umrahSteps.desc: Walk the required lengths between Safa and Marwah. The Qur'an names them among the symbols of Allah.
umrahSteps.tip: Keep your dua and dhikr steady even when the space is crowded.

umrahSteps.title: Trim or shave the hair
umrahSteps.desc: Men shave or shorten the hair; women cut a small amount from the ends. This ends the state of Ihram for Umrah.
umrahSteps.tip: Do not leave this until confusion sets in. It is the closing act of the Umrah.
umrahSteps.ref: Reference: Established Prophetic practice in the rites.

hajjDays.title: Mina
hajjDays.desc: Pilgrims go to Mina and spend the day and night there in prayer and preparation. Tamattu' pilgrims enter Ihram for Hajj on this day.
hajjDays.reminder: Use the day to settle your mind before Arafah.
hajjDays.ref: Reference: The Farewell Pilgrimage sequence in the hadith corpus.

hajjDays.title: Arafah
hajjDays.desc: Standing at Arafah is the central pillar of Hajj. The pilgrim remains within the boundaries of Arafah until sunset in repentance and supplication.
hajjDays.reminder: Missing Arafah is not a small mistake. It is the defining station of Hajj.
hajjDays.ref: Reference: 'Hajj is Arafah' in Sunan Ibn Majah 3015.

hajjDays.title: Muzdalifah
hajjDays.desc: After sunset, pilgrims move to Muzdalifah, combine Maghrib and Isha there, rest, and prepare for the next day.
hajjDays.reminder: Stay with your group safely and keep movement orderly.
hajjDays.ref: Reference: The Farewell Pilgrimage sequence in the hadith corpus.

hajjDays.title: Stoning, sacrifice, shaving, and Tawaf al-Ifadah
hajjDays.desc: Pilgrims stone Jamrat al-Aqabah, arrange sacrifice where due, shave or trim the hair, and perform Tawaf al-Ifadah, with Sa'i where due.
hajjDays.reminder: Some ordering concessions exist in the Sunnah, but specific cases should still be checked carefully.
hajjDays.ref: Reference: Qur'an 2:196 and the Prophetic rite sequence.

hajjDays.title: Days of Tashriq
hajjDays.desc: The pilgrim stays in Mina and stones the three Jamarat on the appointed days while continuing remembrance of Allah.
hajjDays.reminder: The Qur'an allows leaving after two days or staying for a third.

commonMistakes.title: Crossing the miqat without entering Ihram
commonMistakes.desc: This is one of the most common practical mistakes for travellers who are distracted, unprepared, or following a group loosely.
commonMistakes.note: Fixing this can involve more than simply making intention later. Ask a scholar promptly.

commonMistakes.title: Treating crowd pressure as permission to harm others
commonMistakes.desc: The rites do not become more valid because they were done aggressively. Pushing and elbowing at the Black Stone area is not devotion.
commonMistakes.note: Preserving worship and preserving people both matter.

commonMistakes.title: Copying rituals without knowing what is essential
commonMistakes.desc: Many pilgrims imitate others without knowing whether an act is a pillar, a duty, or a recommended Sunnah.
commonMistakes.note: Reference trail: use the guides and hadith anchors on this page instead of crowd imitation.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming every violation invalidates the pilgrimage
commonMistakes.desc: Some mistakes require repentance, some require fidyah, and some affect validity more seriously than others. These are not all the same.
commonMistakes.note: This is exactly where qualified scholarly advice becomes necessary.

healthReadiness.title: Official readiness checks
items: Check current Saudi vaccination and public-health requirements close to departure.
Review whether age, pregnancy, severe illness, or chronic conditions affect your ability to travel.
Keep official booking, visa, and identification records organized before departure.

healthReadiness.title: On-the-ground practical care
items: Hydrate consistently and avoid leaving basic fatigue or heat stress untreated.
Use unscented hygiene items if you will be in Ihram.
Carry only what you can realistically manage in crowds and long walks.
If you are medically vulnerable, speak to your doctor and your scholar before travel.

permissible: Using an umbrella, belt, bag, watch, glasses, and shade.
Bathing and washing with unscented products when needed.
Seeking medical care, rest, and crowd safety.
Reciting Qur'an, making dua, and helping fellow pilgrims.
prohibited: Cutting hair or trimming nails without a recognized excuse and ruling.
Marital relations and conduct leading directly to them.
For men: stitched regular clothing and covering the head.
For women: treating the niqab and gloves as Ihram wear.
Hunting land game while in the sacred state.

spiritualPrep.title: Repair wrongs before travel
spiritualPrep.desc: Return what belongs to people, settle what you can, and ask forgiveness where you have harmed others.
spiritualPrep.ref: A sacred journey should not begin carelessly with neglected rights.

spiritualPrep.title: Learn the rituals before the crowd teaches you badly
spiritualPrep.desc: Study the order, the common errors, and the places where you must stop and ask a scholar.
spiritualPrep.ref: Reference: 'Learn your rituals from me' in Sunan an-Nasa'i 3062.

spiritualPrep.title: Train for patience
spiritualPrep.desc: Crowds, heat, waiting, and exhaustion are part of the test. The heart should prepare for restraint before the body arrives there.
spiritualPrep.ref: Accepted Hajj is tied to upright conduct, not just outward movement.

spiritualPrep.title: Keep the intention simple
spiritualPrep.desc: Do not turn pilgrimage into a performance, travel trophy, or social showcase. Intend worship, repentance, and acceptance.
spiritualPrep.ref: Reference: Qur'an 2:127 as a model dua for acceptance.

faqs.q: What if I miss standing at Arafah?
faqs.a: Standing at Arafah is central to Hajj. A pilgrim who misses it faces a serious validity issue and should seek immediate scholarly guidance about what follows.
faqs.ref: Reference: 'Hajj is Arafah' in Sunan Ibn Majah 3015.

faqs.q: Can I leave Mina after two days?
faqs.a: Yes. The Qur'an allows departure after two days of the appointed days or staying longer without sin when done properly.

faqs.q: Are the short videos enough to learn the rites?
faqs.a: No. They can help you visualize the sequence, but they should not replace the Qur'an, hadith, trusted scholars, and structured written guides.
faqs.ref: Use the short videos only as supplementary refreshers.

faqs.q: Where should I verify health and travel rules near departure?
faqs.a: Check Nusuk and the Saudi Ministry of Health close to your travel date. Do not rely on old screenshots or old group messages.
faqs.ref: Operational guidance can change from season to season.

postHajjSteps.title: Ask for acceptance, not praise
postHajjSteps.desc: The right response after worship is humility and dua that Allah accepted it.
postHajjSteps.tip: Keep the dua of acceptance on your tongue.

postHajjSteps.title: Protect the obligations first
postHajjSteps.desc: The strongest sign of benefit is steadier prayer, better honesty, and more guarded speech when you return.
postHajjSteps.tip: Start with salah, family rights, and daily dhikr.
postHajjSteps.ref: Accepted Hajj should leave a trace in conduct.

postHajjSteps.title: Carry the manners of pilgrimage home
postHajjSteps.desc: Patience, gentleness, and restraint in crowded sacred places should not disappear at the airport.
postHajjSteps.tip: Bring the softened character home, not just souvenirs and stories.
postHajjSteps.ref: Reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i 2622 for the reward of accepted Hajj.

summarySection.title: The page in one clear recap
summarySection.intro: This guide starts with the obligation of Hajj, then walks through Umrah, the major days of Hajj, common mistakes, health readiness, Ihram rules, spiritual preparation, and what should remain after the journey.
points: Hajj is tied to ability, and serious personal cases still need a qualified scholar.
Arafah is the central station of Hajj, while Tawaf, Sa'i, and the order of the major rites must be learned before travel.
Crowd pressure, health neglect, and imitation without knowledge are among the most common causes of mistakes.
Official planning and health checks should be verified close to departure through Nusuk and the Saudi Ministry of Health.
The strongest sign of benefit after Hajj or Umrah is better worship, steadier character, and sincere hope for acceptance.
summarySection.footer: Read the full sections for detail, then return to this recap when you want the essentials quickly.

disclaimer.title: Scope of this page
disclaimer.text: This guide aims to stay close to primary texts, established instructional guides, and official Saudi health and logistics sources. It does not replace a scholar for illness, menstruation, fidyah, missed rites, disputes between madhhabs, or complicated travel restrictions.
items: Hadith anchors used here: Bukhari 1524, Ibn Majah 3015, Muslim 1327, Nasa'i 3062, Nasa'i 2622.
Official operational guidance used here: Nusuk and Saudi Ministry of Health documents current for 1447H / 2026.
disclaimer.warningText: Scholarly approved in practice still means verifying your personal case with a qualified scholar. This page gives the mainstream structure and source trail, not a personalized fatwa.

closing.arabic: رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
closing.translation: Our Lord, accept this from us. You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
closing.message: May Allah grant every pilgrim a sound journey, a valid pilgrimage, and a return marked by humility, gratitude, and firmer obedience.
